document.title: Ten AI tools I tried this year
document.excerpt: I tried many tools this year: an image generator, a meeting summarizer, a coding assistant, and a decision model called Jev that I only tested once. My favourite was the meeting summarizer because it saved me an hour a week.

document.title: Our Jev gate: state, questions and thresholds
document.excerpt: The state holds the contract, a 12k-token section-aware excerpt and provenance. We ask four quality nouls and one role choice. Quarantine happens at P(off_topic) >= 0.8 because precision at 0.7 was 0.67 on one topic; between 0.5 and 0.8 items go to review. Retries: two, jittered backoff from 0.5 s, 20 s deadline per attempt.

document.title: Benchmark: Jev versus cross-encoders on 3 datasets
document.excerpt: We ran 6,234 requests. Table 1: nDCG@10 0.71 (Jev) vs 0.68 (cross-encoder) on SciFact; p50 latency 0.33 s, p95 0.51 s. Code and raw receipts are in the repository.

document.title: Why receipts matter
document.excerpt: Every decision should be replayable from its receipt: the request hash, bank version, reported model, latency, tokens and cost. With receipts, a threshold change never needs a new call, and a model change is visible in the log.
